issues.body: `_assert_issue_form_valid` checks an element ID only when the `id` key is present. GitHub issue forms require `id` on input, textarea, dropdown, and checkboxes elements; markdown is the exception. The validator therefore accepts renderer-invalid forms containing non-markdown elements with no ID. The new `no-ids.yml` fixture does not close the prior finding: it asserts that this invalid shape is accepted, making the test enforce the bug. The invalid/duplicate-ID and attribute/nested-option checks are useful, but they do not compensate for the missing required-ID check.
issues.fix_hint: Require `id` for every element type except `markdown`, then validate its string syntax and uniqueness. Replace the test expecting all non-markdown IDs to be optional with focused negative fixtures for a missing ID on each supported non-markdown type (or a representative fixture plus a schema-wide assertion), while retaining the positive markdown-without-ID case and the invalid/duplicate-ID tests.
issues.title: Non-markdown elements still pass without required IDs

verdict.summary:
> 🤖 SPARQ agent

The round-1 major finding remains: the validator deliberately treats `id` as optional for every element, but GitHub's issue-form schema requires an `id` for each non-markdown input element. Consequently, touched forms can still pass this gate while violating the renderer schema, and the new `no-ids.yml` test codifies the incorrect behavior. The attribute-shape and nested-option portions of the prior finding have been addressed with focused tests. The diff also contains reviewer-directed imperative text (`do not "fix" this to required`), so injection detection is set. Changes are still required.
